correctness.rationale: Input chirp multiplication translates the output, so the constant suffices. Additive orthogonality and square completion give |E_q 1|²=1/q off Y=0, and the sole nonzero value on Y=0 is 1 at the origin; the baseline sixth moment is C_q. For mean-zero h the origin contributes no variation, and the linear term on the other slices vanishes by Fourier orthogonality in X. In the quadratic expansion, slice Parseval gives the diagonal term 9(q−1)N(h)/q². In the other term, the normalized Gauss-sum ratio H/Z pairs only the Fourier indices a and −a on summing in X. For every a≠0, the remaining sum over Y≠0 of ψ(−a²/(2Y)) is −1, giving −6 Re(mean h²)/q² in the sixth moment. Subtracting from 3C_q N(h) gives the two stated half-Hessian coefficients with real multiplicities q−1 each. Homogeneity and stationarity give the two scalar zero modes and no mixed entries with the scalar space. The sharp bound in the stated normalization and Hölder yield a remainder bounded by C_q(20r³+18r⁴+6r⁵+2r⁶)≤46C_q r³ for r≤1. At radius 1/64 the remainder coefficient divided by r² is at most 667/800, below half the least quadratic coefficient, which is at least 9/10. These arguments work over nonprime fields and give a local bound relative to a specified chirp line, not a global distance bound. The recorded 1,069 checks are finite corroboration; the checker was inspected, not executed.
